clues.text: The most Michelin stars ever held in one chef's empire were Daniel Boloud's 21. Alain Ducasse was second with 18, and third place was occupied by this famously foul-mouthed Scot

This fine dining great has gained greater renown for his charity, World Central Kitchen, that feeds victims of disasters in the immediate aftermath

Thomas Keller founded this Napa Valley restaurant, regularly rated the best in America, but which gained additional infamy when Gavin Newsom attended a party there during the peak of the covid pandemic
The chemical term for burning, this word also appears in the classification of traditional gasoline-fired piston engines
This gelled petrochemical was a widely-used incendiary for many years, but its use today is increasingly viewed as a war crime

Widely used in special effects houses because of its bright orange flame, this hydrocarbon is also widely used in home barbecues when you need the grill hot quickly. Hank Hill approves of this question

This fish was re-branded with its Hawaiian name, as people didn't really like eating dolphinfish

This long, thin Italian dagger also lends its name to a type of women's footwear

Thanks for the memories of this legendary host of many an Oscars and USO show. We know he's hitting the links in the sky

clue.text: One of the ancient Olympic sports, it was last won in 1920 by Great Britain's eight-man team, avenging their disqualification in 1912 on the grounds of repeatedly sitting while competing, trying to run out the five minute clock
